steps.label: Finding and Fixing Errors
steps.content:
Algorithms, Pseudocode and Python

Finding and Fixing Errors

Year 8

  • Tell a syntax error from a logic error.
  • Find a logic error by testing with values and tracing.
  • Correct errors in pseudocode and in flowcharts.

steps.label: Two Kinds of Error
steps.content:
Two Kinds of Error

An error in an algorithm is either a syntax error or a logic error.

  • A syntax error breaks a rule of writing the language, such as a misspelt keyword or = instead of <-. The algorithm cannot run at all, and the error message gives the line.
  • A logic error follows every rule, so the algorithm runs, but it gives the wrong output. Nothing tells you which line it is on.

Syntax errors: line 2 and line 3

01  DECLARE Total : INTEGER
02  Total = 0
03  OUTPT Total

Line 2 needs <-; line 3 is misspelt.

Logic error: line 3

01  DECLARE Price, Cost : INTEGER
02  Price <- 4
03  Cost <- Price + 3
04  OUTPUT Cost

Cost should be 3 items at 4 each. It runs, but outputs 7, not 12: line 3 should use *.

steps.label: Check: Syntax or Logic?
steps.content:
Check: Syntax or Logic?

Decide which kind of error each line has.

items.prompt: The algorithm should repeat 5 times. One line is: FOR Count 1 TO 5
items.explain: The arrow <- is missing, which breaks the rules of a FOR line, so the algorithm cannot run.

items.prompt: The algorithm should output "Pass" for a Mark of 50 or more. One line is: IF Mark < 50 THEN
items.explain: The line is written correctly, so it runs, but it sends the wrong marks to "Pass": a logic error.

steps.label: Finding a Logic Error: Test It
steps.content:
Finding a Logic Error: Test It

Purpose: output "Pass" if Mark is 50 or more, otherwise "Fail".

01  DECLARE Mark : INTEGER
02  INPUT Mark
03  IF Mark > 50 THEN
04      OUTPUT "Pass"
05  ELSE
06      OUTPUT "Fail"
07  ENDIF
Test valueShould outputActually outputs
72PassPass
49FailFail
50PassFail
  • For each test value, work out what it should output from the purpose, then trace what it actually outputs.
  • Test a value exactly on the limit (50 here), and one each side. 72 and 49 both look fine; only 50 shows the error.
  • Trace 50 line by line: line 3 asks 50 > 50, which is FALSE. The fix is line 3: IF Mark >= 50 THEN.

Exam Question: Find the Errors

Based on Cambridge IGCSE 0478/23, June 2026, Question 4(a).

01  DECLARE Runners : ARRAY[1:250] OF STRING
02  DECLARE Times : ARRAY[1:250] OF INTEGER
03  DECLARE Index : INTEGER
04  DECLARE RunName : STRING
05  DECLARE RunTime : STRING
06  FOR Index <- 1 TO 250
07      OUTPUT "Enter name, then time in seconds"
08      INPUT RunName
09      OUTPUT RunTime
10      Runners[Index] <- RunMins
11      Times[Index] <- RunTime
12  NEXT Index

What it should do: Store 250 runners' names and times (whole seconds) in Runners and Times. Three errors.

Total: 3 marks

steps.label: Exam Question: Errors That Still Run
steps.content:
Exam Question: Errors That Still Run

Based on Cambridge IGCSE 0478/21, June 2026, Question 7.

01  DECLARE Counter, Total, Number : INTEGER
02  DECLARE Average : INTEGER
03  Counter <- 0
04  Total <- 0
05  INPUT Number
06  WHILE Number > 0 DO
07      Total <- Total + 1
08      Counter <- Counter + 1
09      INPUT Number
10  ENDWHILE
11  Average <- Counter / Total
12  OUTPUT Average

What it should do: Input whole numbers until 0 is input, then output their average, such as 4.5. Three errors.

Total: 3 marks

steps.label: Errors in Flowcharts
steps.content:
Errors in Flowcharts

A flowchart can have the same kinds of mistake. Check it box by box against the purpose.

  • The wrong shape: every box must use the symbol for its job. Ask for or display a value: Input/Output. Store or calculate a value: Process. A Yes/No question: Decision. Start and End: Terminal.
  • The wrong question: a Decision that asks "Is Mark greater than 50?" when the purpose says 50 or more. Test a value exactly on the limit, as with pseudocode.
  • The wrong path: follow the Yes path, then the No path. Each must do what the purpose says for that answer.
  • A missing input: "Display the value of Age" before Age has been asked for. A value must be input before it is compared or used.

steps.label: Check: Errors in Flowcharts
steps.content:
Check: Errors in Flowcharts

Two flowchart errors to find.

items.prompt: A flowchart should display "Pass" for a Mark of 50 or more. Its decision asks "Is Mark greater than 50?". Which Mark shows the error?
items.explain: 50 should pass, but "Is 50 greater than 50?" is No, so it goes down the wrong path. Every other value gets the right answer.

items.prompt: A flowchart box "Store Price * Quantity in Cost" is drawn as a parallelogram. Which symbol should it be?
items.explain: Storing a calculated value is a Process, drawn as a rectangle. A parallelogram is for asking for or displaying a value.

The line is written correctly, so the algorithm runs. Is its output right?
